name: engraving
title: Copperplate engraving
summary: A natural-history plate that engraves itself: swelling burin lines build a figure by hatching, labels are cut letter by letter, and a hand-laid wash brings it to colour.

look.ground: laid cream paper with a pressed plate mark and a ruled border; the sheet is the world

palette.where: paper in the vignette and foxing
one warm near-black for every line
transparent earth or mineral wash, one stronger pigment at most

look.type: roman capitals (Bodoni Moda) cut glyph by glyph for titles and labels, italics for scientific names, Pinyon Script written in one stroke for notes and subtitles on a deckled slip
look.texture: all tone is line density: swelling and tapering hatch lines in up to three crossing families; no grey fill
look.light: one light from the upper left for the whole film; tone from the shape, never from texture
look.materials: intaglio ink on paper; copper and burin when the making is shown

consistency: one subject on one plate, built up and then annotated with numbered roundels

motion.feel: cutting order is the animation: outline, hatching, crossing, darks; colour blooms last
moves: burin-speed line cutting, dozens of hatch lines at once
roundels fly in on an eased arc and grow to size
lettering cut glyph by glyph, script written left to right
watercolour blooms from one point with a drying wet rim

pace.text: script subtitles on a paper slip, at most two lines; an engraved note stays chars/12 + 1 s

banned: opaque colour or colour on lettering
copying a real plate, pose or border
source: LemoLab's Copperplate Engraving style in lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar at 9eb7739; pace measured with analyze.py and events.py on its demo film "The Honeybee, Plate VII"
